questions.explain: The chapter establishes a standing rule: no training extract may include a Highly Confidential column unless it passes through an approved de-identification stage, enforced by running the classification catalog query as a pipeline gate.
options: Only columns with Dynamic Data Masking applied
Columns labeled Highly Confidential, unless they pass through an approved de-identification stage
Only columns in the dbo schema
Columns larger than 1 GB in storage size
questions.q: According to the chapter, which columns must never appear in a training extract without first passing through a de-identification stage?

questions.explain: The HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 clause is the k-anonymity floor: it guarantees no feature row describes fewer than 50 individuals, neutralizing the most common re-identification path for aggregate features.
options: To reduce query execution time
To satisfy the differential privacy epsilon budget
To enforce a k-anonymity floor so no feature row describes fewer than 50 individuals
To compress the result set for the feature store
questions.q: In the differential-privacy feature aggregation example, what is the purpose of the HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 clause?

questions.explain: Deterministic tokens preserve joinability — the same customer maps to the same token across extracts — while the one-way SHA-256 hash makes re-identification computationally infeasible.
options: Deterministic, irreversible tokens that preserve joinability across extracts
Reversible encryption so analysts can look up raw values on demand
Plaintext passthrough with audit logging only
Random UUIDs regenerated on every extract
questions.q: What tokenization approach does the chapter recommend for direct identifiers in row-level training extracts?

questions.explain: Federated learning inverts the pipeline: each SQL Server instance trains locally inside its own security boundary and only model weight updates travel back to the coordinator, so no row ever leaves its home instance.
options: Centralizing all regional data into one lake before training
Encrypting the training data with Always Encrypted during transit
Training one model per site and deploying them independently with no coordination
Training locally on each SQL Server instance and sharing only model weight updates with the coordinator
questions.q: How does the federated learning pattern in the chapter handle training data that cannot leave its jurisdiction?

questions.explain: Always Encrypted with secure enclaves lets rich computations run inside a protected enclave where even a sysadmin cannot observe the data, while column master keys stay in Key Vault or an HSM under the data owner's control.
options: Storing the column master keys on the database server for convenience
Using secure enclaves so computations run on encrypted data, with keys held in Key Vault or an HSM outside SQL Server
Disabling attestation so queries never fail
Granting UNMASK permission to the data science service account
questions.q: What is the recommended key-custody arrangement for Always Encrypted with secure enclaves in ML pipelines?
